n: Right after the suffering Servant, Zion is pictured as a childless woman who is told to sing, because she will end up with more children than a married wife. The Savior quoted this entire chapter to the Nephites (3 Nephi 22), saying “great are the words of Isaiah.”

Make your tent bigger—stretch the curtains, lengthen the ropes, drive the stakes deeper—so there’s room for all the children. Latter-day Saints took the word “stakes” from this verse for local Church units that strengthen Zion.

f.g: The fabric walls of a tent.

n: Zion will spread out in every direction; her descendants will possess the nations and fill once-empty cities.

f.w: thy seed shall inherit the Gentiles

n: Don’t be afraid or ashamed. You will forget the shame of your youth (bondage in Egypt) and of your widowhood (exile).

f.g: The disgrace of seeming abandoned—Israel in exile.

n: Why? Because your Maker is your Husband—the Lord of Hosts, your Redeemer, the Holy One of Israel, God of all the earth. The covenant is pictured as a marriage, with the Lord as a faithful Husband.

f.w: The God of the whole earth

n: The Lord calls her back like a young wife who was abandoned and heartbroken.
“For a brief moment I left you, but with great compassion I will bring you back.” The time of separation is short compared to the mercy that follows.
In a flash of anger God hid His face for a moment, but His mercy is everlasting kindness. The Hebrew word ḥesed means loyal, covenant love.

f.g: Hebrew ḥesed ‘olam—eternal covenant love and loyalty.

f.w: I hid my face from thee

n: Just as God swore after Noah’s flood never again to flood the earth, He swears never again to be angry with or rebuke His people this way. His covenant is as sure as the rainbow.
Mountains may move and hills shift, but God’s loving kindness and covenant of peace will never be removed. One of the strongest promises in scripture.

f.w: my kindness shall not depart from thee

n: To storm-battered, uncomforted Zion, God promises to rebuild her with beautiful stones and sapphire foundations.

f.g: Probably lapis lazuli, a deep blue stone.

n: Her towers and gates will be made of gems. John’s vision of the New Jerusalem echoes this jeweled city.

f.g: Carbuncles = glittering red stones; the Hebrew word suggests sparkling.

n: All her children will be taught by the Lord and enjoy great peace. Jesus quoted this to teach that those who come to Him are taught by God.

f.w: all thy children shall be taught of the LORD
great shall be the peace of thy children

n: Zion will be firmly established in righteousness, free from oppression and terror.

f.w: In righteousness shalt thou be established

n: If anyone gathers to attack her, it won’t be by God’s doing, and the attackers will fall.
God created the blacksmith who forges weapons and the destroyer who uses them. Since He is over both, nothing can happen to Zion outside His control.
A famous promise: no weapon made against God’s servants will succeed, and every accusation against them will be answered. This is their inheritance, and their righteousness comes from God.

f.w: No weapon that is formed against thee shall prosper
